response_change.parent_relation: The target mapping dI_dt(Q,I,P_pol) uses a single polarization memory state with one relaxation time, so the restoring contribution from dielectric memory has one characteristic lag and a correspondingly single-dispersive dependence on oscillation amplitude/phase.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the single-timescale polarization assumption by a two-timescale conservative dielectric memory in which an additional slower reversible polarization state contributes to the effective restoring charge. Then dI_dt depends on both fast and slow internal polarization coordinates, producing a richer non-separable curvature of dI_dt versus (Q,I) through history-dependent state mixtures reachable from the same observation protocol.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding capacitance, inductance, and existing saturation scales fixed while varying polarization relaxation scales near and above the nominal LC period, the child can show a broader, two-stage lagged restoring response: for similar instantaneous Q and I, early-cycle versus later-cycle accelerations differ because slow polarization has not yet equilibrated. A parent with one shared relaxation time can match either the fast-lag or slow-lag curvature but not both across these conditions.

plan.activation_condition: Visible when dielectric relaxation is neither instantaneous nor frozen: polarization relaxation time comparable to the nominal LC period, and the added slower branch would be several times larger than that but still within the observed time window; initial polarization must be small but nonzero so memory is actually excited.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, single-branch memory already creates phase-lagged restoring shifts. In holdout, adding a slower reversible branch extends this into a two-stage lag/curvature effect over longer portions of the trajectory, especially when charge amplitude is large enough that capacitor saturation and delayed polarization interact.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the added slow polarization branch has zero coupling, zero initial excitation together with invariant zero dynamics, or relaxation time collapsing to the existing branch so the two branches act effectively as one.
plan.promotion_reason: A genuinely distinct dielectric relaxation channel is an internal dynamic degree of freedom, not a static parameter tweak. Existing states cannot represent simultaneous fast and slow reversible polarization memory, so one additional state is needed to create an observable change in the scored target mapping rather than only reparameterizing the current branch.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes all reversible dielectric memory is captured by one polarization coordinate with one relaxation timescale, which is an idealization for many dielectrics that exhibit distributed or at least multi-timescale polarization response even in low-loss conditions.
plan.baseline_assumption: Internal dielectric polarization responds with a single Debye-like relaxation time and a single saturating restoring contribution.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Add a second reversible polarization channel representing a slower bound-charge rearrangement that contributes to the effective restoring charge without dissipation, yielding conservative multi-timescale dielectric memory.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-timescale dielectric-memory assumption rather than add dissipation or forcing, because the benchmark explicitly targets conservative electromagnetic exchange. The parent target law maps observed states to dI_dt through one lagged polarization contribution, so at fixed instantaneous Q and I it effectively permits only one characteristic phase relation between polarization memory and charge. Varying conditions means comparing trajectories where the nominal LC timescale sqrt(inductance*capacitance) is held fixed, existing initial Q and I are held at their contract values, and dielectric-memory timescales are in the scientifically admissible regime comparable to or somewhat larger than the LC period. Under those conditions, a child with both fast and slow reversible polarization can produce a measurable contrast: the current acceleration for similar Q and I differs between earlier and later oscillation segments because the slow branch accumulates and releases restoring charge on a different timescale. That is a changed target mapping, not merely a hidden auxiliary effect, because dI_dt itself would depend on an additional observable internal state not reducible to the existing single P_pol branch. A single parent parameter refit cannot generally absorb this across the admissible regime: changing polarization_relaxation_time or polarization_coupling only shifts one lag scale and one saturating branch, so it cannot simultaneously match both the short-lag response near the start and the delayed curvature emerging after several fractions of an LC cycle when a second memory branch remains out of equilibrium. This refinement stays within the conservative scenario, preserves bounded charge/current through saturating storage terms, and has a clear parent-recovery limit if the added branch decouples or collapses onto the original one.

embedding.description: Use a finite-capacity, saturation, threshold, or regime-transition response.
